simple.meaning: דָּם (dâm) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “blood (as that which when shed causes death) of man or an animal; by analogy, the juice of the grape; figuratively (especially in the plural) bloodshed (i.e. drops of blood).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 361 times across Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, beginning at Genesis 4:10. Its contexts include family, blood, wilderness.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דָּם (H1818).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: דָּם (dâm) / H1818 is traced through Genesis 4:10, Genesis 4:11, Genesis 9:4, Genesis 9:5 as a generated source-based concept entry.
